Accuracy is 1.0 pp short of the 0.753 bar. Both measurements fell inside my ranges.

How time arises. time ≈ fixed cost + epochs × 48 steps × per-step cost.
- Fixed cost is about 0.2-0.4 s: copying 150 MB uint8 to the GPU, the fp16 cast, reflect padding, eigendecomposition on 5k images, and first-step allocator growth. That is under 5% of the run, so H3 and H3.2 are weak levers.
- Per step, the run is GPU-bound. Conv FLOPs dominate, then memory-bound BN, GELU and residual elementwise ops at fp16.
- The 4-CPU pin barely matters, because batch 1024 makes each step long compared with launch latency.
- steps_per_epoch = 50000 // 1024 = 48, so the port already drops the ragged batch. Every train step has the same shape, and I006 has nothing to fix.
- Expected levers:
  - torch.compile fusing BN+GELU+add: 12-22% per step.
  - Fused or foreach SGD: about 1-2%.
  - CUDA graphs: under 3%.
  - Progressive resizing cuts FLOPs to about 0.75× over the epoch average. Small-resolution layers use the GPU less efficiently, so real savings are about 12-18%.
- The masked 25-way crop loop in augment costs about 25 launches per epoch, which is negligible.

- buy back accuracy with roughly free regularisers, such as Lookahead/EMA, worth about +0.2-0.4 pp;
- add epochs, about 10% time each;
- remove time per epoch with compile.

The net order is compile first, then epochs. Anything that cuts information per sample costs accuracy roughly in proportion:
- lower resolution, which also adds a train/test resolution mismatch;
- larger batch, which means fewer updates.

Muon at batch 2000 halves the update count. On CIFAR-10, Muon gains have been about 10-15% in steps, and I doubt that fully offsets halving the updates at 9 epochs on 100 classes.

- per-seed accuracy std about 0.2-0.35 pp, so the std of the 3-seed mean is about 0.15-0.2 pp;
- run-to-run time drift about 1-2%.

At that noise level, effects of 0.2 pp are unresolvable from a single 3-seed run. To be safe over 40 seeds, the 3-seed mean should be at least 0.755.

structured_output.world_model:
W1 (mechanism), after E001.

What was measured. E001 is the airbench96-style port: eager mode, fp16, channels_last, data resident on the GPU, 9 epochs, LS 0.3, no TTA. It reached 0.7430 accuracy in 9.43 s per trial, about 1.0 s per epoch plus a few tenths of a second fixed cost. That is faster than my eager prior of 1.1-1.4 s per epoch. Accuracy is 1.0 pp short of the 0.753 bar. Both measurements fell inside my ranges.

How time arises. time ≈ fixed cost + epochs × 48 steps × per-step cost.
- Fixed cost is about 0.2-0.4 s: copying 150 MB uint8 to the GPU, the fp16 cast, reflect padding, eigendecomposition on 5k images, and first-step allocator growth. That is under 5% of the run, so H3 and H3.2 are weak levers.
- Per step, the run is GPU-bound. Conv FLOPs dominate, then memory-bound BN, GELU and residual elementwise ops at fp16.
- The 4-CPU pin barely matters, because batch 1024 makes each step long compared with launch latency.
- steps_per_epoch = 50000 // 1024 = 48, so the port already drops the ragged batch. Every train step has the same shape, and I006 has nothing to fix.
- Expected levers:
  - torch.compile fusing BN+GELU+add: 12-22% per step.
  - Fused or foreach SGD: about 1-2%.
  - CUDA graphs: under 3%.
  - Progressive resizing cuts FLOPs to about 0.75× over the epoch average. Small-resolution layers use the GPU less efficiently, so real savings are about 12-18%.
- The masked 25-way crop loop in augment costs about 25 launches per epoch, which is negligible.

How accuracy arises. At 9 epochs CIFAR-100 is sample-starved, and accuracy sits on the steep part of the curve. I estimate about +0.6 pp per extra epoch near 9-10 epochs, so 0.753 needs about 10.5-11 epochs on the eager recipe, which would take about 11 s. The realistic path is:
- buy back accuracy with roughly free regularisers, such as Lookahead/EMA, worth about +0.2-0.4 pp;
- add epochs, about 10% time each;
- remove time per epoch with compile.

The net order is compile first, then epochs. Anything that cuts information per sample costs accuracy roughly in proportion:
- lower resolution, which also adds a train/test resolution mismatch;
- larger batch, which means fewer updates.

Muon at batch 2000 halves the update count. On CIFAR-10, Muon gains have been about 10-15% in steps, and I doubt that fully offsets halving the updates at 9 epochs on 100 classes.

Noise. These are priors, not yet measured:
- per-seed accuracy std about 0.2-0.35 pp, so the std of the 3-seed mean is about 0.15-0.2 pp;
- run-to-run time drift about 1-2%.

At that noise level, effects of 0.2 pp are unresolvable from a single 3-seed run. To be safe over 40 seeds, the 3-seed mean should be at least 0.755.

What I'm unsure of:
(a) the real accuracy slope per epoch, which I002 measures;
(b) how much max-autotune helps convs that cuDNN already autotuned; the gain may come only from fusion;
(c) whether the port has a subtle loss of accuracy compared with the reference airbench96. Two possibilities are the whitening eps and the lr 9.0 scaling at batch 1024. If such a bug exists, a free +0.5-1 pp is available.

forecasts.reason: Port is below the bar, so this goes 9→10 epochs: about +10% time and about +0.4-0.8 pp, which fits the per-half-epoch slope in H4.2.1.
Fusing the memory-bound BN/GELU/add ops cuts per-step time by about 15%; the math is unchanged and there are no recompiles because all train shapes are fixed.
Lookahead/EMA likely adds +0.1-0.4 pp at about 1-3% time; the gain is near the noise floor and the time cost sits near the 2% line.
GPU-bound with fixed shapes, so time drift should be about 1% and per-seed std about 0.2-0.35 pp.
There is no ragged batch: n//bs means the port already drops it, so the change saves well under 0.3 s.
Batch 2000 halves the update count to about 225 steps; Muon's per-step gains probably don't make that up, so it stays below 0.753 at 9 epochs.
About 25% fewer FLOPs gives about 13% less time, but less information per sample plus the resolution mismatch costs more than 0.2 pp in a 9-epoch sample-starved regime.

cruxes: What is the accuracy slope per epoch near 9-11 epochs (I002)? This decides whether reaching 0.755 costs about 1.5 epochs or 3.
How much of the 1.0 s per epoch is memory-bound elementwise work that compile can fuse, versus cuDNN conv time? This sets the I003 gain and the final time.
Is the port losing accuracy against reference airbench96 (whitening eps, lr/wd scaling, BN eps 1e-12 in fp16)? If so, fixing it gives a free +0.5-1 pp that could avoid adding epochs.
